title: List the classes a newer runtime will refuse

blocks.text: The search team built its query library on Java 22 and tried out a preview feature in one class. Three other services use the library, and the platform team now plans to move all of them to Java 24. Last time, a service reached production and failed to start with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`. This time a check runs over every jar first and lists the classes the target runtime would refuse.
`ClassFileCheck` already reads the bytes of each class file and builds the report. Finish the three `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/ClassFileCheck.java`:

items: `release(...)`: the Java feature release a class was compiled for;
`usesPreview(...)`: whether it was compiled with preview features enabled;
`loads(...)`: whether a runtime of a given release, started with or without `--enable-preview`, accepts it.

blocks.text: `u2(...)`, `minorVersion(...)` and `majorVersion(...)` read the header for you. About six lines in total.

cases.says: a class compiled by this build for Java 21 is reported as release 21, without preview
headers of Java 8, 17 and a Java 22 preview class are reported with their release and preview mark
classes compiled without previews load on their own release and every later one, and a class from a newer release is refused
a Java 22 preview class loads on Java 22 started with --enable-preview
a Java 22 preview class is refused by Java 23 and 24 even with --enable-preview
a Java 22 preview class is refused by Java 22 started without --enable-preview

origin.section: A Preview Class File Runs Only on the Release That Compiled It

concepts: A class file that uses preview features (minor version 65535) loads only on the release that compiled it, while an ordinary class loads on its release and every later one.
